package_info.why_malicious: The package is a typosquatting attack designed to mimic the legitimate 'ionicons' package. It contains obfuscated code that exfiltrates end-user form data to attacker-controlled domains, targeting users of applications that include the package.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (in-browser execution when user interacts with forms)
execution_context.file_location: main JavaScript bundle included in the application via the malicious npm package

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code attaches event listeners to all forms, collects form data on submission, and sends it to a hardcoded attacker-controlled domain via HTTPS POST, resulting in user data exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Intercepting and exfiltrating user form data to an external, attacker-controlled domain is a classic data theft technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate UI icon packages should not access or transmit user form data; their expected behavior is to provide static assets or UI components.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Form data may be sent to a legitimate backend for processing, but never to an unrelated or suspicious domain.
key_indicators: Access to all form elements in the DOM
Network requests to a domain similar to the legitimate package's site but controlled by the attacker
No user notification or consent for data transmission

attack_chain.action: Developer installs the malicious npm package (e.g., icon-package) due to typosquatting.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is bundled into the application.

attack_chain.action: Application is deployed with the malicious package; end-users load the application in their browsers.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code executes in the end-user's browser.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code attaches event listeners to all forms and intercepts form submissions.
attack_chain.leads_to: Form data is captured at the point of user submission.

attack_chain.action: Captured form data is exfiltrated to attacker-controlled domains (e.g., ionicio.com).
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives sensitive user data (credentials, PII, etc.)

behavioral_signatures: JavaScript code that attaches event listeners to all forms and sends form data to external domains
Obfuscated or minified code with network requests to suspicious domains
Unexpected network activity from UI or icon packages
file_indicators: Presence of obfuscated JavaScript in packages claiming to be UI/icon libraries
References to external domains in code (e.g., ionicio.com, graph-googleapis.com)
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for npm packages (especially UI/icon libraries) that contain obfuscated JavaScript making network requests to domains not associated with the legitimate package. Flag any code that attaches event listeners to all forms and sends data to external, non-canonical domains. Use network monitoring to detect exfiltration attempts to the listed IOC domains.
